content:
Alice Nguyen: thinking about a safer path for automated node isolation when GPUs report transient ECC/Xid spikes.
Alice Nguyen: current autodrain flow is too eager for short bursts — causes unnecessary task churn and capacity loss.
Raj Patel: +1. we've seen 3 short ECC bursts this week that resolved after thermal throttling cleared :face_with_thermometer:
Mei Hernandez: proposal: two-stage action: 1) soft-taint (no new pods) + attach ticket/annotation 2) escalate to drain after persistent errors for N minutes or error-count threshold
Tomasz Kowalski: how do we avoid thundering-herd on drain restart? e.g., many pods reschedule onto same rack.
Olivia Brooks: add an eviction score that includes node load, rack dispersion, and recent drain count. prefer nodes with spare capacity in other racks.
Raj Patel: also include model priority / SLA in score so prod-critical jobs don't get bounced repeatedly.
Alice Nguyen: example flow shorthand:
```
- signal: ECC or Xid spike (>5 events / 1m)
- immediate: `kubectl taint node <n> gpu-unstable=true:NoSchedule` (soft)
- wait: 10m window with rolling dedupe
- if persisted: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` or Slurm: `scontrol requeue` / `sinfo` fallback
```
Mei Hernandez: need debounce + exponential backoff; if same card clears and then flips again multiple times, escalate to replace rather than keep draining.
Tomasz Kowalski: we must capture hardware telemetry (ECC counts, PCIe errors, temperature) and map to node-id in alerts. sre-bot should include a compact summary to drive automation.
sre-bot: Alert: gpu-node-512 ECC count spike: 12 in 60s, temp=84C, PCIe retries=3. Annotating node with `gpu-health:ecc`.
Olivia Brooks: automation should annotate runbook link and recent deploys so oncall can decide to step in before replacement.
Raj Patel: one more constraint: some regions (apac-prod) have limited spare capacity — prefer local soft-taint but do not auto-drain unless cluster-sim says safe.
Alice Nguyen: good point. we need a capacity-check step in the orchestrator: query cluster capacity, reserved pools, and then decide action tier: soft-taint / migrate low-priority / hard-drain / replace.
Mei Hernandez: sample JSON policy for orchestrator:
```
{
  "signal_types": ["ECC","Xid","thermal"],
  "soft_taint_duration": 600,
  "error_threshold": 8,
  "persistence_window": 900,
  "region_safe_drain": ["us-west-2","eu-central-1"],
  "fallback_policy": "route-to-dedicated-or-hosted"
}
```
Tomasz Kowalski: Slurm integration: if node is in exclusive GPU partition, we should `scontrol update NodeName=<n> State=DOWN Reason="gpu-err"` and let sched requeue or reassign per policy.
Olivia Brooks: ops playbook:
- if soft-taint clears -> remove taint, annotate incident resolved
- if persisted -> initiate maintenance job and mark for replacement
- when replacing, avoid simultaneous replacements in same rack
Raj Patel: metrics to surface in Console: per-node ECC time-series, recent drain events, replacement count, and an "unreliability score" (0-100)
Alice Nguyen: UX: show suggested action in Console with one-click approve (auto, canary, manual) + preview which workloads will be moved.
Mei Hernandez: implementation notes:
- orchestrator runs as deployment with leader election
- integrates with telemetry pipeline (prometheus -> push rules)
- writes ops annotations and opens a ticket in incident tracker via infra-operator-bot
infra-operator-bot: Created ticket INF-3248: gpu-node-512 ECC spike. Suggested action: SOFT_TAINT. Link: https://issues.redwood.example/INF-3248
Tomasz Kowalski: edge-case: GPU ECC counters can reset on reboot. need to persist historical counters in TSDB to catch flapping over longer windows.
Raj Patel: testing plan: simulate ECC bursts on a canary pool, verify soft-taint -> recover path and persistent -> drain -> replacement path. include Slurm + k8s mixed clusters.
Olivia Brooks: cost consideration: each unnecessary drain increases job runtime and egress (rescheduling heavy models). factor that into the eviction score as penalty.
Alice Nguyen: next steps: Mei + Raj to draft orchestrator config and scoring function. Tomasz to list Slurm commands for maintenance flow. Olivia to draft Console UX mock for approvals.
Mei Hernandez: I'll post a short RFC with config schema and test harness next week :calendar:
Raj Patel: thanks — will work on canary tests.
Alice Nguyen: cool. low-priority ask: add thermostat thresholds to telemetry so we can suppress actions for thermal-only spikes that correlate with scheduled CPU-heavy jobs.
Olivia Brooks: noted.
Mei Hernandez: tagging this as action items: @Raj Patel @Tomasz Kowalski @Olivia Brooks — we'll sync in infra sync tomorrow :eyes:
Alice Nguyen: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
